annotations.target_phrase: Bronze by gold heard the hoofirons, steelyringing.
annotations.annotation_text: The famous polyphonic opening chord of Episode 11 (Sirens). 4:00 PM. Set in the Ormond Hotel bar on the Liffey quays. 'Bronze' represents the bronze-haired barmaid Lydia Douce; 'gold' represents Mina Kennedy. The first sixty lines form a musical overture announcing all acoustic themes developed across the episode.
sources: Gilbert, Stuart. James Joyce's Ulysses: A Study. Faber, 1930.
Gifford, Don, and Robert J. Seidman. Ulysses Annotated. UC Press, 1988, p. 288.

annotations.annotation_text: Acoustic deformation of 'impertinent insolence', mimicking the rhythm and dissonance of musical notes sounding together in a fugue ('fuga per canonem').
sources: Budgen, Frank. James Joyce and the Making of Ulysses. 1934.
Kenner, Hugh. Ulysses. Johns Hopkins UP, 1987.
